PCR‐DGGE analysis of clonal T cell receptor γ gene rearrangement can be useful for the diagnosis of cutaneous lymphoproliferative disease.
PCR‐DGGE analysis of TCRγ gene can be useful for the differential diagnosis of cutaneous lymphoproliferative diseases.

the PCR‐based strategy is a useful tool for detection of clonality of cutaneous T cell lymphomas, and the PCR‐DGEE method is very useful in the differential diagnosis of cutaneous lymphoproliferative diseases.

the development of a PCR‐DGGE‐based strategy for analysis of clonality in cutaneous T‐LGL, and the results of our study indicate that this approach is useful for diagnosis of cutaneus T‐cell neoplasm.
the development of a PCR‐based strategy for analysis of T‐cell receptor (TCR) gene rearrangements in the diagnosis of cutaneous lymphoproliferative diseases.
the analysis of the TCRγ gene in the diagnosis of cutaneous lymphoproliferative diseases.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PCR‐DGEE method is a useful tool for diagnosis of cutanous T‐cell neoplasm.

PCR‐DGGE analysis for TCRγ gene is useful for the diagnosis of cutaneous lymphoproliferative diseases, especially for cases with a histologically difficult diagnosis, but that this method should be used in conjunction with other diagnostic methods such as histopathology and immunohistochemistry.
PCR combined with denaturating gradient gel electrophoretic analysis of T‐cell receptor genes is a very helpful tool in the differential diagnosis of cutaneous lymphoproliferative diseases.

clonal T‐cells are not necessarily neoplastic.

the PCR‐DGCE technique can be applied to fresh frozen skin biopsy samples and is useful to detect clonally expanded populations of T cells in the skin, and thus can contribute to the differential diagnosis of cutaneous lymphoproliferative diseases.
